title: Xetodus, an indie browser based 3D space MMO
author: AgreeableEstate4958
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’ve been working on **Xetodus** and wanted to share it here.

You can fly between star systems, land on planets to build colonies, and touch down on moons to drill for resources. Explore and build up your colony, work toward a better ship, or head out looking for a fight. There’s both PvP and PvE combat.

The universe has **750+ procedural star systems**, with **20+ ships to fly** and **17+ skills to max level** and get on the ranking leaderboards!

Everything runs in your browser. No download or launcher needed. It’s free to play with an optional "Vanguard" membership.

[**https://xetodus.com**](https://xetodus.com/)

Would love to hear what fellow AI engineers and game devs think! Questions, things that need work, stuff you’d like to see added, let me know! I been receiving overwhelming positive feedback on this, and appreciate any and all feedback to make this even better.

  
For the AI workflow side:

I am a single engineer  
I built a custom harness that outperforms all other harnesses (OMP, Hermes, Openclaw, etc.) called Cybara (https://cybara.ai) fully open source and all providers supported.  
I use frontier models and my decades of engineering experience to produce everything you see.

comments.author: JorgitoEstrella
comments.body: This is like the 8th space game in this sub in just s few days but this looks better than at least 6 of them, nice job.

comments.author: Sufficient-Bid3180
comments.body:
I've started playing this 2 days ago and neither the video or description does this game justice.

It's not quite EVE Online in a browser, but already has more content than what EVE Echoes or Second Galaxy launched with. 

You can seamlessly switch between EO's semi-automatic combat and EVE Frontier (or any other dogfighting sim's) full control flight, you can arm yourself with various types of guns, missiles and support equipment, each taking fixed hardpoints or moving turrets that make positioning and manouvering matter more than giving you x% chance to take less damage.

Mining and industry is fully featured, allowing players to manufacture about 95% of all items in the game, including all ship hulls. You can build colonies on actually LANDABLE planets for passive income. There's also dynamic PvE events and static anomalies.

The game feels like one of those Kickstarter pitches that offer an insane amount of content, except it's already playable and free.

Finally, the dev is actively reading discord and ingame chat, and we are getting patches so large daily that you see other games take a month to push out. This game singlehandedly made me realize how much i was underestimating AI game dev.
